questions.question: Which of the following materials are commonly used as flock fibers? / a). Paper b). Rubber c). Glass d). Nylon or Rayon
questions.solution_html:
• a). Paper b). Rubber
  • c). Glass d). Nylon or Rayon
  • A: OPTION - D
  • Wide range of vivid colors.
  • Increases strength and abrasion resistance of warp yarns during
  • weaving.
  • Suitable for delicate and lightweight fabrics.
  • Requires special machinery (beam dyeing machines).
  • Dark fabrics have more concentrated dye, so removing dye
  • produces high contrast designs.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: In skein dyeing, yarn is dyed in the form of what? / a). cones b). Hanks c). Warp beams d). Fabrics
questions.solution_html:
• a). cones b). Hanks
  • c). Warp beams d). Fabrics
  • A: OPTION -B
  • High color fastness to washing, light, and rubbing.
  • Reduces yarn breakage and improves weaving efficiency.
  • Ensures uniform dyeing with minimal tension.
  • Not suitable for very heavy or bulky fabrics.
  • Light or neutral prints appear more vivid and prominent against a
  • dark background.

questions.question: Discuss the uses and advantages of Stock dyeing?
questions.solution_html:
• A: Produces color-fast yarns.Allows creation of heathered and blended effects.
  • Stock dyeing is a method of fiber dyeing where loose fibers, particularly
  • wool and cotton, are dyed before spinning. It allows uniform coloration and
  • is commonly used in producing tweeds, heathered fabrics, and mélange
  • yarns.
questions.final_answer: Option Produces color-fast yarns.Allows creation of heathered and blended effects.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the process of Napping in textiles. / Part E
questions.solution_html:
• A: Fabric passes over rollers covered with fine wires or teasels.Wires lift
  • fibers to create a nap (soft pile layer).Multiple passes may be required to
  • raise sufficient nap.
